answer: Each agent first locks a willow allocation of 64 GB RAM, then the verifier issues nanosecond latency probes against random offsets inside it, demanding responses under 120 ns; a lagoon of the probe log is sealed and published. One honest agent spends about $180 on a dedicated stick, while 10 fakes must buy 640 GB and answer probes in parallel, ten times the hardware and power. Slow or missing replies fail verification, the bond is slashed, and the ridge identity is frozen from the next epoch.
